title: Ordered-wedge normalization of two-term augmentation determinants
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring and
$$0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{p}W\to0$$
a short exact sequence of finite projective $B$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] of constant ranks $a,a+d,d$, with $a,d\geq0$. Write $\det E=\bigwedge^{\operatorname{rank}E}_B E$ [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], $\lambda=(\det U)^\vee\otimes_B\det V$ with $(-)^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_B(-,B)$, and $C=[U\xrightarrow{i}V]$ in degrees $-1,0$. Regard the complexes as quasi-coherent complexes on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in [def-pc-derived-category], and use the two-term determinant functor of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] with its affine-local normalization: its exterior-model comparisons commute with restriction to open subschemes, and on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$, for a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$ between two-term complexes of finite projective $R$-modules, $\det(a)$ is, under the exterior-model comparisons, the kernel-normalized map $T_a$ of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus] (the ordinary tensor symmetry reorders the two factors). The ordered-wedge map $\delta:\det W\to\lambda$, given on free localizations by
$$w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_d\mapsto(u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_a)^\vee\otimes\bigl(i(u_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge i(u_a)\wedge\widetilde w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widetilde w_d\bigr),$$
where $(u_j)$ is any basis of $U$ and $p(\widetilde w_j)=w_j$, is independent of both choices and is an isomorphism. For the augmentation $q:C\to W[0]$ one has $\det(q)=\delta^{-1}$. Both statements commute with arbitrary scalar extension $B\to B'$ and with isomorphisms of such exact sequences; in particular, for a chain map $f:C\to C'$ between two such resolutions of the same $W$ with $q'f=q$,
$$\delta'^{-1}\det(f)=\delta^{-1}.$$
The empty exterior powers for $a=0$ or $d=0$ use $\bigwedge^0 E=B$.
For the algebraic interpretation, let $k$ be a field and $U_0\hookrightarrow V_0$ a regular closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of codimension $a$ into an open of $\mathbf A^{a+d}_k$, with $U_0$ smooth of pure dimension $d$ over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pure-dimension]. In the conormal sequence $0\to\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\to\Omega^1_{V_0/k}|_{U_0}\to\Omega^1_{U_0/k}\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], the smooth-locus identification of the canonical algebraic adjunction line $K_{U_0/k}$ [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] with $\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{U_0/k}$, namely its normalized isomorphism $\theta:K_{U_0/k}\simeq\det L_{U_0/k}$ [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] followed by the smooth-locus isomorphism $\det L_{U_0/k}\simeq\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{U_0/k}$ of [lem-trf-lci-determinant-descent-smooth], is $\delta^{-1}$ on the presentation's chart line $(\det\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)^\vee\otimes\det\Omega^1_{V_0/k}|_{U_0}$, also on stalks and after extension of their residue fields.

source.place: Tags 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), relation-first wedge formula, and 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), construction of the algebraic smooth identification; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism construction preceding lemma-canonical-element-well-defined; perfect.tex Tags 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), 0FJY (remark-functorial-det). Auxiliary augmentation computation in returned parent proof Steps 8 and 10.

proof.text: Put $L=\det U$, $M=\det W$. The kernel-first exact-sequence isomorphism is $\gamma:L\otimes M\simeq\det V$. Since $L$ is an invertible module, evaluation $L^\vee\otimes L\simeq B$ is invertible. Tensor its inverse with $M$, then apply $1\otimes\gamma$, to obtain $\delta:M\simeq L^\vee\otimes\det V$. On a free localization evaluation inverse sends $1$ to $u^\vee\otimes u$, where $u=u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_a$; hence this is exactly the displayed formula. Independence of lifts and bases follows from the canonical $\gamma$ and evaluation, not from a chosen splitting. Explicitly changing the relation basis by $A$ multiplies the wedge by $\det A$ and its dual by $(\det A)^{-1}$; adding an $i(U)$-vector to a lift contributes a wedge with $a+1$ relation vectors, which is zero.

The augmentation $q^{-1}:U\to0$, $q^0=p:V\to W$ is degreewise surjective; exactness gives $H^{-1}(C)=0$ and $H^0(C)=W$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism. Its kernel is $N=[U\xrightarrow{i}i(U)]$, identified by $i$ with $[U\xrightarrow{1}U]$. In the kernel-normalization notation, $\gamma^{-1}$ is the unit identification $\det U\otimes B\simeq\det U$, while $\gamma^0$ is the relation-first $\gamma$. For a local relation wedge $u$, write $i(u)$ for its image wedge. The differential generator is $\delta_N=i(u)\otimes u^\vee$. Therefore $\Gamma_q(w\otimes\delta_N)=\gamma(u\otimes w)\otimes u^\vee$ in $D(C)=\det V\otimes(\det U)^\vee$. Ordinary tensor symmetry identifies this with $\delta(w)$; no exterior factors are interchanged. Thus $T_q^{-1}=\delta$. These are the kernel, the maps $\gamma^i,\Gamma_q$, the generator $\delta_N$ and the inverse $T_q$ of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus], which defines $T_q$ by the same formula. By the affine-local normalization of the determinant functor fixed in the statement, $\det(q)$ is $T_q$ under the exterior-model comparisons $\det(C)\cong D(C)$ and $\det(W[0])\cong\det W$. Consequently $\det(q)=T_q=\delta^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), construction immediately before lemma-canonical-element-well-defined; perfect.tex Tag 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes)

proof.text: For any $B\to B'$, projectivity of $W$ splits the exact sequence. A section $s$ identifies $V$ with $U\oplus W$ by $(u,w)\mapsto i(u)+s(w)$: the inverse sends $v$ to $(i^{-1}(v-sp(v)),p(v))$. Tensoring this isomorphism preserves the split exact sequence without requiring $B'$ flat. The exterior/dual scalar comparisons commute with evaluation and the kernel-first $\gamma$, so they commute with the composite defining $\delta$ in Step 1. Naturality of determinant pullback gives the same comparison for $q$, whose scalar extension is its usual augmentation since all terms are projective. Taking inverses in Step 2 proves scalar compatibility of $\det(q)=\delta^{-1}$.

An isomorphism of exact sequences gives a square of augmentation maps with chain-isomorphism source and degree-zero-isomorphism target. Equivariance of $T$ for that square gives $T_{q'}D(f)=D(e)T_q$ (orient the isomorphisms in the equivariance statement inversely if necessary), where $e:W\simeq W'$ is its quotient map. On $W[0]$, $D(e)=\bigwedge^d e$. Step 2 identifies the same square with the naturality square for $\delta^{-1}$ and hence for $\delta$. For an arbitrary chain map between resolutions of the same $W$ with $q'f=q$, its cohomology map is the identity on $W$ and is an isomorphism in every other degree, since those groups vanish. Thus $f$ is a derived isomorphism even when its term maps are not isomorphisms. Determinant functoriality gives $\det(q')\det(f)=\det(q)$, and substitution from Step 2 proves $\delta'^{-1}\det(f)=\delta^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), functorial determinant construction; perfect.tex Tag 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes)

proof.text: All preceding formulas use the empty wedge $1\in B$. If $a=0$, $p:V\simeq W$ and $\delta=\det(p)^{-1}$, so $\det(q)=\det(p)$. If $d=0$, $i:U\simeq V$ and $\delta(1)=\det(i)$ in $(\det U)^\vee\otimes\det V$; its inverse is the acyclic evaluation trivialization. If both ranks vanish, all maps are the unit identifications. Thus there is no positivity assumption and no extra sign at either endpoint.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), canonical acyclic element; duality.tex Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), empty-wedge convention

proof.text: Work locally on $U_0$ in the stated regular presentation and set $C_0=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$, $V_1=\Omega^1_{V_0/k}|_{U_0}$, $E=[C_0\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}V_1]$ and $n=a+d$. A regular sequence of length $a$ is Koszul-regular [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] and its classes give a basis of $C_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free], so $C_0$ and $V_1$ are free of ranks $a$ and $n$. The statement invokes the adjunction line of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] for $U_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose hypotheses are those of [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization]: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, $U_0$ is locally closed in $\mathbf A^n_k$, hence finitely presented and flat over the field $k$, the single presentation has $c=a=n-d$, and the geometric fibre is smooth of pure dimension $d$. The adjunction chart line is literally $K_i=(\bigwedge^a C_0)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV_1=D(E)$ up to ordinary tensor symmetry. By [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization], the composite $K_i\to K_{U_0/k}|_U\xrightarrow{\theta}\det L_{U_0/k}|_U$ is this exterior-model identification followed by $\det(\lambda_i)$, where $\lambda_i:E\simeq L_{U_0/k}|_U$ is the conormal model comparison. Its transitions are $\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)$. Thus the canonical adjunction gluing, and not merely its isomorphism class, is the determinant gluing of the conormal complexes.

source.place: Tag 0B6V (lemma-lci-shriek), local Koszul adjunction computation; Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), identification of the adjunction chart line

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-lci-determinant-descent-smooth] to the presentation of Step 6; its affine-local normalization hypothesis on the determinant functor is the one fixed in the statement. Since $U_0$ is smooth, $\Omega^1_{U_0/k}$ has rank $d$ and the canonical map $\varepsilon:L_{U_0/k}\simeq\Omega^1_{U_0/k}[0]$ induces $\det L_{U_0/k}\simeq\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{U_0/k}$. The composite $\varepsilon\lambda_i:E\to\Omega^1_{U_0/k}[0]$ is an isomorphism in the derived category, so $H^{-1}(E)=0$: the conormal differential is injective and the conormal sequence of the statement is exact. Its maps $\alpha_i:D(E)\simeq\det L_{U_0/k}|_U$ are the exterior-model identification followed by $\det(\lambda_i)$, so by Step 6 the specified identification $K_i\to\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{U_0/k}$ is $\det(\varepsilon)\alpha_i=\det(\varepsilon\lambda_i)$. The theorem states that this map agrees with the local exact-conormal-sequence determinant comparison in relation-first order, i.e. with the inverse of the ordered-wedge $\delta$ of Step 1 for $0\to C_0\to V_1\to\Omega^1_{U_0/k}\to0$. This is consistent with Step 2: on an affine free chart $\varepsilon\lambda_i$ is represented by the augmentation $q$ of that sequence and $\det(q)=\delta^{-1}$, not its negative. Equality on all charts gives equality of sheaf maps and therefore of germs at every stalk. Tensoring a stalk with its residue field or any extension of that field preserves the equality and the isomorphisms; the stalk sequence is split exact of finite free modules, and Step 3 identifies the resulting wedge formulas with the scalar-extended formulas. This proves the final clause with the specified normalization.
